status: confirmed by the user with revisions; six logistic-regression fits authorized
question: do video features improve scoring of sparse videos in random exposures, and does personalization add value beyond them?
evidence_role: KuaiRand-1K random validation is development data; results are exploratory; random test is not used
task: pointwise P(long_view = 1 | exposure), evaluated on random exposures
training_data: standard training exposures 2022-04-07 to 04-21 (5.02M rows, labels long_view)

feature_timing.training_rows: every statistic for a training exposure at time t uses only standard training events with time < t (same-timestamp events excluded), computed in time order; the smoothing prior p0 is also the global long-view rate before t (0.25 when no history)
feature_timing.evaluation_primary: history frozen at training cutoff T for L1, L2, and iALS alike: statistics use training events only; decayed counts are aged to the exposure time and hours since the last long view use the exposure time, which adds no new information
feature_timing.limitation: training rows see fresh history while evaluation rows see history frozen at T (fixed-deployment setting)
feature_timing.rolling_variant: not run in this round; a later secondary experiment only
feature_timing.out_of_catalog_videos: only exposure-time fields (metadata attributes, logged duration, upload age at exposure); missing history statistics take zero counts, the prior rate, and missing flags

L1_non_personalized: logged duration (log, <=18 s flag, zero flag)
video age at exposure (log days; missing flag)
video_type AD flag, upload_type, music_type, primary tag (top 50 + other)
video before-t stats: log exposures, log long views, smoothed long-view rate (beta prior, strength 20), decayed long views (tau 0.5 d, 2 d), log hours since last long view (missing flag)
L2_personalized: user before-t: log exposures, smoothed long-view rate
user x author before-t: log long views, smoothed long-view rate on that author
user x primary tag before-t: share of the user's long views with that tag, smoothed long-view rate on that tag
duration match: |log duration - mean log duration of the user's past long views|, user's share of long views on <=18 s videos
levels.L3_reference: frozen time-decay iALS (five seeds) score x_u . y_v; videos outside its catalog score 0

model.type: logistic regression per level with intercept
model.objective: mean binary log loss over training rows + l2 * ||beta||^2 (intercept unpenalized); l2 is a penalty strength, not an inverse C
model.scaling: numeric features standardized with training-row mean and SD
model.categoricals: upload_type levels with >= 1000 training rows, music_type levels, primary tag top 50 by training rows; other values -> other, missing -> missing; levels fixed on training rows
model.selection: mean log loss on standard-validation exposures of tuning-half users (seed-2028 split), features frozen at T

evaluation.scope_A_primary: known users, random-validation exposures of videos in the training catalog: L1, L2, iALS (five seeds, per-user AUC averaged over seeds)
evaluation.scope_B: known users, all random-validation exposures including videos outside the catalog: L1, L2 only
evaluation.users: per-user AUC users (both outcomes) are recounted within each scope; every paired comparison uses identical users and exposures
evaluation.primary: scope A per-user AUC: L2 - iALS
evaluation.key_ablation: scope A per-user AUC: L2 - L1
secondary: scope B per-user AUC: L2 - L1
pooled AUC by video group (outside catalog, degree 0, 1-2, >= 3) with user-cluster bootstrap
standard-validation report-half session GAUC for context
evaluation.statistics: paired user bootstrap 2000 resamples seed 2026; sample sizes reported with every interval
evaluation.interpretation: if L1 beats iALS but L2 does not beat L1, conclude that video attributes and statistics help, not that personalization helps

decision_rule: no single significant subgroup declares success; the 27K independent-user confirmation is judged from the primary and key-ablation effect sizes, interval widths, and feasibility; a practically meaningful per-user AUC gain is pre-specified as +0.01 (about 14% of popularity's 0.073 margin over chance)
confirmation_27k: conditional: download Pure/27K, verify ID correspondence and overlap with the 1K users, isolate unused users, freeze the method, retrain on their standard logs; confirms reproducibility on new users in the same period, not future generalization
